key_insight: SANA-Video 2.0 shows that high-quality video generation can be scaled efficiently with a hybrid attention design, matching full-softmax video models while keeping the long-sequence efficiency of linear attention. It can generate up to 720p video on a single GPU using one unified architecture at 5B and 14B scales.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high compute and memory cost of video diffusion transformers, especially the quadratic cost of full attention on long video sequences. It aims to make high-resolution video generation practical without sacrificing quality.
method: Uses a unified hybrid video diffusion transformer architecture instantiated at both 5B and 14B parameter scales.
Combines gated linear attention for efficient O(N)-dominated token mixing with periodic gated-softmax attention anchors to preserve global coherence.
Introduces attention residuals to reduce the quality drop typically seen when replacing full-softmax attention with linear attention.
impact: This work makes high-resolution video generation more accessible by reducing the compute burden while maintaining strong visual quality. For practitioners, it points to a practical path toward scalable, single-GPU video synthesis models.

paper_title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
paper_authors: Junsong Chen, Jincheng Yu, Yitong Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu
